restrictions: Target sha256-r31-prefix-v1: SHA-256 compression steps 0..30 inclusive on every padded block, standard fixed IV once at the start, FIPS 180-4 padding, full feed-forward, full 256-bit big-endian digest; ordinary collision of two distinct finite byte strings.

The online algorithm is a DETERMINISTIC REPLAY of exactly the two 128-byte messages written in proof.md Section 3 (first block M0 shared; second blocks differ only in words W5..W9). It performs no random draws and no search, so its algorithmic success probability is exactly 1 and there is no trial-count, amplification, matching, or completion-rate term in the cost argument.

PROVENANCE: the collision and the matched prefix are the attributed published Li-Liu-Wang / Li-Liu-Wang-Dong-Sun results; finding the first block is the published practical attack's work, not ours. The construction is fully specified in proof.md (signed condition table, exact message/expansion differences and constants, exact admissible sets V5..V8/G16/G18/S, Phase-1 table equations, Phase-2 first-block match, capped Phase-3 completion), so no external paper is needed to audit the algorithm.

COMPLETE LEDGER: the whole collision construction is charged once as preprocessing and inside total time, at the published complexity, with no cross-target amortization and no parallel wall-time discount. The published 2^40.5 is already expressed in 31-step SHA-256 compressions, which is the collision-frontier-v5 unit, so no publication-to-v5 conversion or CPU-second calibration enters the bound.

time_log2 is a hard upper bound that holds on every run: the construction is <= 2^40.75 (published 2^40.5 with a <1.19 disclosed-extras allowance) and the deterministic replay is <= 2^2.67 units, so their sum is <= 2^40.75 (the replay is negligible), and no probabilistic step exists.

Memory is a reported metric only, with no scalar contribution and no tie-break, and is NOT a declared heuristic. baseline_improved = sha256-r31-nominal-v2 is a required reference identifier and does not assert an improvement.

The certificate is the published 31-step collision pair, re-hashed by the organizer; the only nonuniform advice the online algorithm consults is that stored 256-byte pair. No organizer experiment is requested.

heuristics.statement: The one-time cost of constructing a sha256-r31 colliding pair of the specified two-block shape is at most the published 31-step practical-attack complexity, ~2^40.5 target-compressions (already in the v5 unit); with a factor 2^0.25 allowance for the authors' disclosed additional work the construction is at most 2^40.75. Adding the strictly positive deterministic replay (<= 2^2.67) gives a total below 2^40.75 * (1 + 2^-38.08) < 2^40.7501, so the total charged time is bounded by 2^40.76 target-compression units.
heuristics.scope: The one-time published collision construction (characteristic, matched first block M0 with carried words W0..W12, and completion to a colliding pair) that underlies the replayed certificate, plus the deterministic online replay. The matched prefix is the attributed published result; our re-completion of W13..W15 reuses it and is covered by the published term. Not a per-call or amortized attack cost.
heuristics.extrapolation: The load-bearing evidence is a cited literature figure plus the organizer-verified certificate, not any measurement of ours. The published Li-Liu-Wang 31-step practical attack has complexity ~2^40.5 expressed in 31-step SHA-256 compressions, which is exactly the collision-frontier-v5 unit, so it is charged directly with no conversion factor; its dominant cost is the first-block search that produced M0. The organizer-verified certificate demonstrates that a colliding pair of this construction exists on the exact target. The construction term is 2^40.75; the replay adds <= 2^2.67, and their sum is below 2^40.7501 < 2^40.76.
heuristics.limitations: A published complexity figure is not an organizer-model instruction trace, so this qualifies exploratory plausibility but not rigorous qualification. The ~2^40.5 is the authors' reported practical-attack complexity; because it is already in compression units no unit conversion is applied. Sensitivity: only if a reviewer places the construction materially above 2^40.75 target-compressions would time_log2 need to rise. No CPU-second calibration or participant measurement affects the bound.
